correctness.rationale: First-divergent-run argument proves t<delta injectivity; an explicit two-pattern bridge collision exists at delta and extends through n-1 using common remaining capacities. Coefficientwise smoothing maximizes the deletion-pattern bound over fixed total/run count, and cycling q>=t+1 distinct run letters attains it; sharpness follows from n=r=t+1 and at most q one-letter descendants. All ranges including r=1 and t=n-1 are addressed. Independent exhaustive short finite checks corroborate, but do not replace, these all-parameter proofs.

value.rationale: The first-collision cost is a natural exact structural invariant for when the standard pattern-counting upper bound is tight. It supplies infinitely many exact optimal values for the nondivisible-run deletion problem explicitly left open in recent literature, with q>=t+1 a demonstrably sharp uniform sufficient threshold. This includes r>q, where letters repeat and pattern collisions could otherwise arise; its use is not restricted to one arbitrary numerical slice.
